newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares dive 2.42 pct on cash shortage.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares dive 2.42 pct on cash shortage.

text.p: Istanbul shares lost an average 2.42 percent in thin trade on Monday due to afternoon selling sparked by a lack of liquidity influx following narrow range-trade in the last few days, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,532, down 38 points from Friday, but rebounded slightly from a late low of 1,516. It had gained 1.2 percent last week.
Trade volume firmed to 20.66 trillion lira from 19.24 trillion on Friday.

"There wasn't any specific reason behind the sharp afternoon fall. There is no liquidity influx and political uncertainties discourage players from keeping share positions," said Murat Aktas from Yasar investment.
"Volume is low, so sales pressure may continue and pull the index below the 1,500 support," said Aktas.
Brokers do not expect any liquidity influx before an upcoming holiday next week because investors in Turkey traditionally invest in state securities over long holidays.

A 4-1/2-day religious holiday between April 17-21 will be followed by an official holiday on April 23. The government has declared April 22 holiday for public offices, but it is not yet known if the markets will be closed.

Of the 242 shares traded, falls sharply outdid rises by 196 to 18 and 28 finished stable. The IMKB Industrial dived 2.61 percent to 1,527, the IMKB Services shed 1.71 percent to 1,438 and the IMKB Financial lost 2.32 percent to 1,643.
Top actives were utility Cukurova Elektrik, down 2,500 lira at 217,500 and state oil refiner Tupras, down 1,000 lira at 63,00. They made up about 20 percent of the total turnover.
